limitations: The registry proves declared ownership only; automation internals outside the finite evidence set are unproved and require black-box adapter acceptance.
supported_claim: The canonical registry contains exactly 25 sequence rows and names each row's folder, automation display, pass signal, operation kinds, and lineage; one row is explicitly a non-standalone sub-sequence and several rows name multiple or external automation components.

limitations: It does not automatically intercept host actions and does not define registered-use, raw-dispatch, prevented-failure, or system-wide overhead denominators.
supported_claim: EVENT_FIELDS is a closed event schema for run, blocker, correction, transition, verification, operation context, execution claim/return, and observer events; build_parser exposes typed lifecycle commands, while --context-file, --argv-json, --request-json, and several free-text CLI fields remain raw file/string boundaries. summarize/_metrics reports run quality and repeated blockers but not the required system-wide enforcement metrics.

limitations: The guard is opt-in and command-string based; it cannot prove that every action reaches it.
supported_claim: cmd_activate binds selection receipts and hashes; cmd_guard validates a voluntarily supplied command string against sequence_doc, discovery_log, script, or tool_help provenance and contains bounded correction-bootstrap checks.

limitations: It is an opt-in Bash/subprocess wrapper, accepts arbitrary remainder argv, and has no host-wide interception authority.
supported_claim: run performs guard, durable execution_claim, subprocess.run(argv), and durable execution_return for one exact argv, with source-repository binding.

limitations: Fingerprint recording does not itself prohibit a later execution or dispatch a verified successor.
supported_claim: normalize_error_signature and fingerprint produce stable blocker fingerprints; cmd_open records first occurrence or recurrence and cmd_transition advances the blocker state.

limitations: It observes after execution, may fail safely without rolling back the closed run, and links reuse evidence but does not force future dispatch.
supported_claim: observe_committed_run reconstructs a candidate from one closed governed run, selects LINK_REGISTERED/LINK_DISCOVERY/PROPOSE_DISCOVERY/NO_CANDIDATE, persists decision/link/bootstrap events, and is invoked automatically by work_memory run-close only when operation context exists and the observer is enabled/auto.

limitations: Input is still supplied through a JSON spec file and the controller starts discovery but does not own the complete promotion/reuse lifecycle.
supported_claim: normalize_spec validates an exact discovery bootstrap object; bootstrap atomically/idempotently creates the discovery bundle, classification/selection/activation receipts, and deterministic run-start identity.

limitations: The lifecycle begins after a discovery exists, uses command strings/JSON CLI parsing, and does not force later compatible actions to select the promoted sequence.
supported_claim: cmd_drive owns qualification, promotion, registered same-path verification, and correction-required stops; _verify_run uses guarded shlex-split shell execution and records verification/closure; status is recomputed from documents and ledger rather than a single durable transition journal.

limitations: Checkpoint completion is path-keyed, external lifecycle effects are reconciled by current state, and no common effect-identity journal spans branch changes or all sequence owners.
supported_claim: cmd_execute and cmd_execute_rolling use an approval-gated disposition manifest and a checkpoint keyed by manifest hash; cmd_drive verifies the current bundle and runs the guarded rolling controller.

limitations: This durable protocol covers promotion only, is not a common transition/effect journal, and does not establish branch-safe multiple-run ownership for other operations.
supported_claim: cmd_promote uses a PREPARED/APPLYING/COMMITTED journal, crash recovery, atomic target replacement, registry insertion, and promotion/transition ledger events.

limitations: This is one representative sequence, not the system-wide owner, budget, resume, or metric implementation.
supported_claim: ResearchDriver is one typed Operation-enum controller with PREPARED/COMMITTED effect reconciliation, single-writer lock, resume-token-bound frozen inputs, package reconciliation, and interval metrics. admit_round reserves 3*(role_timeout+grace) despite five mandatory roles and omits materialization, terminal work, and retry allowance from initial admission; retry uses a later heuristic. Metrics subtract role time and expose mechanical_ratio but have no event-classified exclusion contract or real governed-corpus gate.

limitations: The second run still executes the seed sequence before the observer links the registered sequence; the test does not prove pre-action selection, mandatory reuse, recurrence prevention, system-wide coverage, or real-run overhead.
supported_claim: test_observed_candidate_traverses_real_lifecycle_then_reuses_registered proves a synthetic local path from observed closed run to proposed discovery, two qualifications, promotion, registered verification, and a later observer LINK_REGISTERED decision.

limitations: This evidence does not prove exact-once external effects, a common journal with memory-knowledge, branch ownership, or crash tests across every transition.
supported_claim: WorkflowStateStore atomically saves/loads per-run JSON and persists durable_generation, last_durable_transition, last_durable_phase_id, approval checkpoint, phases, fan-out items, and histories.

limitations: It proves a potential Claude structural-withholding surface and a missing Codex one in this translator, not that every host supports or enforces withholding.
supported_claim: translate_to_claude builds explicit allowed tool names, including Task/WebSearch/MCP/Bash; translate_to_codex returns only sandbox and approval_policy and does not construct a per-tool withholding manifest.

limitations: The documentation supplies no pre-dispatch coverage for subagent launch or non-MCP remote paths; those classes therefore require structural withholding or a future host-owned hook, otherwise visible unsupported failure.

limitations: Requirements define required outcomes but do not prove current implementation.
